author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Why shader translation is a core shadPS4 compatibility frontier
summary: The video-core sources document a translation pipeline that must convert PS4 GPU programs into host-compatible shaders while preserving memory and numeric behavior.
heroAlt: Gameplay screenshot distributed in the official shadPS4 repository
searchKeywords: Why shader translation is a core shadPS4 compatibility frontier

blocks.text: Decode begins with AMD GCN instructions

PS4 graphics programs are encoded for AMD GCN hardware, so shadPS4 first needs an instruction-level frontend rather than a source-language compiler. `frontend/decode.cpp` and `frontend/opcodes.h` identify guest operations; instruction and control-flow files turn branches into a structure the later compiler can traverse. A decode failure is concrete: an opcode, encoding field or branch target was not represented correctly before Vulkan entered the picture.
Scalar, vector and memory operations enter an intermediate representation

The translation layer is split by behavior: scalar ALU and flow, vector ALU and interpolation, scalar and vector memory, exports and data-share operations. Those translators emit shadPS4 IR instead of writing SPIR-V directly. Keeping a stable IR lets optimization and legalization passes reason about shared memory, barriers, resource tracking and control flow without duplicating the guest decoder in every host backend.
IR passes prepare code for the SPIR-V backend

The `ir` tree contains blocks, instructions and passes that simplify or rewrite operations before host emission. The SPIR-V backend then handles integer, floating-point, image, atomic, barrier, composite and subgroup behavior in focused emitters such as `emit_spirv_image.cpp` and `emit_spirv_shared_memory.cpp`. A missing GCN behavior may therefore be fixed in decode, translation, an IR pass or final emission; those are different failure stages.
Shader output still depends on video_core state

A correctly emitted SPIR-V module can render the wrong result if image formats, buffer bindings, samplers or guest memory are wrong. `video_core` supplies those resources through its texture and buffer caches and constructs Vulkan pipelines around the shader. Conversely, a validation message at pipeline creation can reveal an invalid interface produced by the compiler. Debugging has to follow the shader and its bound state together.
Logs and captures should identify the first bad stage

A useful report records the exact scene, title update, shadPS4 revision, GPU and driver. A screenshot establishes the symptom; a shader dump, compiler log or RenderDoc capture can show whether decode failed, SPIR-V was rejected, a resource was unbound or pixels diverged only after a later pass. Changing resolution, HDR, FSR and several experimental options at once destroys that comparison, so the baseline should stay narrow.
